sources.text: In the study, students read a short passage. One group read it again; the other group wrote down everything they could remember. Five minutes later the re-reading group did slightly better. One week later the recall group remembered clearly more.

Retrieval practice means pulling information out of memory, for example by answering a question or writing what you remember. Re-reading, highlighting and reviewing a summary put the information in front of you again without asking you to recall it.
The benefit was measured on the same passage the students had studied. Whether it transfers to new problems was not tested in this study.
